clue.text: Compliments to the ladies for making real, lasting reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the preceding words are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the two words supply all eleven letters

explanation.surface: A man pays women flattering remarks in the hope of changing his ways for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantries are courteous attentions or flattering speeches a man pays to women, the old sense of gallant as a ladies' man.

clue.text: Good, mature terrier even worked as a gun dog

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: worked as in kneaded or manipulated, so those letters are moulded into another order

parts.note: mature in years means old
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog fancier admires a well-bred older terrier that once did a gundog's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The terrier in the surface is only letters; the dog actually defined is a different breed altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden retriever was bred to fetch shot game for hunters, which is exactly what a gun dog does.

clue.text: Relief to be allowed out of bed

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
someone up has risen from bed

explanation.surface: A patient is relieved at last to be allowed to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off in something unpleasant, a respite from pressure.

clue.text: Participate in public sale? Upper class indeed!

parts.note: surface padding: it frames the clue as a question about joining in
read as 'in deed': a deed is an action, and 'in' puts the upper-class letter inside it
U is the abbreviation for upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether bidding at a public sale is a posh pastime, and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be read as two words, 'in deed': the U goes in a word for deed, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a sale open to the public in which goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Thanks for fine cheesecloth

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
split as cheese plus cloth: feta is a Greek cheese, and the cloth half is the definition

explanation.surface: A grateful note for a delicate length of cheesecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheesecloth' looks like one word for the definition, but it splits into a cheese and the cloth that is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often silk, used for dresses.

clue.text: Soul is represented in manner

indicators.note: represented in the sense of presented again in another form, so the letters reappear rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's true spirit shows in the way they behave.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a person's spiritual or mental nature, the self behind outward behaviour.

clue.text: Introvert psychiatrist's vigil: note problem

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist; the 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: a problem is something troubled or awry, signalling that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A therapist notes that a shy patient has trouble staying up through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is an idiom for a very shy, retiring person who avoids attention.

clue.text: Our rap makes terrible racket!

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rapper admits that their music is just an awful noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud, confused din or commotion, just as a racket is.

clue.text: Select chunky dish to be replaced by girl

indicators.note: being replaced means one part of the word is swapped out and another goes in its place

parts.note: taken as written, the word to be altered
dish and hunk are both slang for an attractive person
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A chef chooses to swap a hearty dish for one a young woman prefers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is not food here but slang for a good-looking man, the part removed from the middle of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means exclusive or high quality, which is what classy means.

clue.text: Prudent overwork landed one top career

parts.note: split as over plus work: op is short for opus, a work, and over turns it round
lit means alighted or landed, as a bird does
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter only

explanation.surface: An overworked executive has just secured a top job, a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwork' must be split into two words, 'over' and 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic as an adjective means wise and judicious in action, the same as prudent or shrewd.

clue.text: Wake student after playtime

indicators.note: after tells us one piece follows the other in order

parts.note: split into play, giving FUN, and time, giving ERA
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A pupil is woken up after break at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' looks like a verb about waking a student, but it is the noun for a vigil over the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake is a gathering held around a death, closely tied to the burial ceremony itself.

clue.text: Make dear Eric prove potential

indicators.note: potential suggests what the letters could become, another arrangement of them

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants a fond friend to show what he is capable of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make dear' reads as endearing someone; here dear means expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To overprice something is to set its cost too high, making it expensive.

clue.text: Published thousands of files

parts.note: a newspaper that ran a story published it
K is a thousand, so thousands are Ks

explanation.surface: A printer has released thousands of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'files' looks like documents but means rows of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranks and files are both lines of soldiers drawn up side by side or one behind another.

clue.text: Bloody unusual

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of meat, lightly cooked and red inside

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a British expletive, 'bloody unusual'; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak cooked briefly is still red and bloody, and something seldom seen is uncommon.

clue.text: Panic about a town's lack of power

indicators.note: about in the sense of turned around and about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
a town and a city are both urban places; the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: A blackout causes alarm across a town without electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacity is an inability to act or function, a want of strength or capability.

clue.text: Fed up, having made a mistake, and was put off

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone sick of things slipped up and was postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as bored, but 'up' turns the first word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deferred has been postponed to a later time.

clue.text: Pregnant woman saw girl coming in with notes

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim
her refers to a girl
B and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: An expectant mother spotted a young woman arriving with some written messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is not the past of see but a noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother-to-be is a woman expecting a baby, who will become a parent on its birth.

clue.text: Threaten with bad name at church

indicators.note: bad as in spoilt or corrupted, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar warns a parishioner that a bad reputation at church will follow them.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to intimidate them with a show of hostility.

clue.text: Rotation imparted, which takes head off skittle

parts.note: to top a plant or vegetable is to take its head off
skittles are the pins knocked down in bowling

explanation.surface: A spinning bowl decapitates a skittle.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward spin given to a ball by striking it above centre, making it dip and kick on bouncing.

clue.text: Lower down mountain river is lost from the land

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: something lost from a word has dropped out of it

parts.note: the earth is the dry land
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mountain stream disappears below the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath is a preposition or adverb meaning below, at a lower level.

clue.text: Grew up, having coped with him leaving

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: to cope is to manage
him refers to a man

explanation.surface: Someone matured after dealing with a partner walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: To have aged is to have grown older, to have matured over time.

clue.text: Soak some children chasing us

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following text is used

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Kids running after us with water pistols leave us wet through.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench something is to wet it thoroughly, to saturate it.

clue.text: Unsophisticated backwater

parts.note: split as back plus water: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water, and back turns it round

explanation.surface: A rural backwater is described as simple and unworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwater' is one word in the surface but splits into a reversal signal and a brand of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and lacking worldly experience, the opposite of sophisticated.

clue.text: Pattern made from cut up rubbish

indicators.note: up here signals the preceding word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a snip is a cut
tripe is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A design has been made from shredded waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a fabric design of very thin parallel lines, as on a banker's suit.

clue.text: Fresh broth for a pound?

indicators.note: fresh as in new, so the letters are made over into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Soup made today on sale for one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like the British currency but is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat with a strong rhythm, as a heart pounds.

clue.text: Revolution's holding against Queen's conspiracy

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so pieces go within the outer word

parts.note: a coup is a revolutionary seizure of power; the 's means is
V is short for versus, against
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A rebellion opposed the monarch's secret plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up is a concerted effort to hide wrongdoing, which is a kind of conspiracy.

clue.text: Material with Lycra mix, initially in colour

indicators.note: to mix is to stir things together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A fabric blended with stretchy Lycra, first available in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Lycra is a trademark stretch fibre, used here only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre and the fabric woven from it.

clue.text: Yorkshire addiction for backing the horses?

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three ridings
a habit is an addiction

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman's gambling problem is betting on horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing the horses' suggests betting, but here it means sitting on a horse's back; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding habit is a woman's traditional outfit worn when mounted on a horse.
